origins.section: A Vertex Is Where Two Boundary Lines Cross Inside the Region
The Objective's Level Lines Are Parallel, and the Best Plan Is the Last Point the Line Touches
If an LP Has a Best Plan, Some Vertex Is a Best Plan

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-corner: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-corner: A **vertex** (a corner) of the region is a feasible point where two boundary lines cross. ... A crossing is a vertex only if it is feasible: two lines can cross somewhere every plan is forbidden.
recorded.prompt:q-level: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-level: So the picture method is: draw one level line through the region, then slide it in the direction $`(5, 4)`$, keeping it parallel, until one more nudge would leave the region. The last feasible points it touches are the best plans. (Values: (0,0)=0, (0,4)=8, (3,3)=15, (4,0)=12.)
recorded.prompt:q-tie: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-tie: Now the level lines are parallel to the budget line $`d + t = 30`$, and the line comes to rest along the whole edge from D to C. Every plan on that edge, such as $`(11, 19)`$, is optimal with value 120. (Summary: "Several vertices can tie, and then the whole edge or face between them is optimal.")

recorded.prompt:q-corner:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-corner:a: "A crossing is a vertex only if it is feasible: two lines can cross somewhere every plan is forbidden."
recorded.prompt:q-corner:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-corner:c: "A **vertex** (a corner) of the region is a feasible point where two boundary lines cross" and "A crossing is a vertex only if it is feasible". Two tight rows are not enough when the point breaks another row.
recorded.prompt:q-corner:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-corner:d: "Two lines ... meet at one point unless they are parallel." The stem says x = 5 and y = 5 cross at (5, 5), so they are not parallel. Only the stem and this passage together rule d out.
recorded.prompt:q-level:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-level:a: "Distribution is the better buy per dollar, so the obvious answer is 'all of it to distribution'. That answer is wrong, because two more rules apply". Here (4,0) is worth 12, less than 15 at (3,3).
recorded.prompt:q-level:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-level:b: By the level-line rule, (0,4) is worth 8 and is not the last point touched. No passage addresses "y at its largest" reasoning directly, so this is the rule applied.
recorded.prompt:q-level:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-level:c: "it cannot come to rest on a point in the middle of the region, because from there it could slide further." (2,2) is not a corner and lies inside the region.
recorded.prompt:q-tie:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-tie:b: "Every plan on that edge, such as $`(11, 19)`$, is optimal with value 120."
recorded.prompt:q-tie:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-tie:c: "A linear objective's value at a weighted average is the same weighted average of the vertices' values": the midpoint is worth 55.
recorded.prompt:q-tie:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-tie:d: "An LP solver returns one optimal plan; when there are several, which one it returns is up to the solver."
